result.summary: ConfigParser::process_array() now accepts short `[ ... ]` arrays as well as `array( ... )`. This works at the top level, for nested values, for keyed values, and when the two syntaxes are mixed. The closing token (']' or ')') is tracked for each array level, and no eval() is used. I added tests/Unit/ConfigParserUnitTest.php with 6 tests (the two required inputs, mixed syntax, empty `[]`, unclosed '[', and '[' closed by ')'), and they pass with PHPUnit run by hand. The gates named in the task do not exist in this worktree: there is no `check-fast` or `check` composer script, no phpunit.unit.xml, no tests/bootstrap.php and no config_inc.php or database. So I could not run them, and the status is partial. As a stand-in, I ran every data and error case from tests/Mantis/ConfigParserTest.php directly against the parser without a database: 53 cases, 0 failures.

changes.summary: Accept '[' as the start of an array in parse(), for nested elements and for keyed values; process_array() matches ']' or ')' depending on how the array was opened.
New unit test (no core.php or DB needed) for short arrays: constants as key and value, nested, mixed with array(), empty, unclosed '[' (expects Exception), and mismatched closing token.

acceptance.criterion: ConfigParser::parse() returns array( NEW_ => REPORTER ) for "[ NEW_ => REPORTER ]" and array( 'a' => array( 1, 2 ) ) for "[ 'a' => [ 1, 2 ] ]".
